# The colength↔degree identity on the WIDENED adaptation, with NO separation hypothesis

`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffFieldDegree.lean` ports the *support-separated* colength↔degree identity
to `AffAdaptation`.  That route works, but its `hsep` is a real restriction and it has no
producer: a `work-reviewer` audit this session closed a refutation showing that `hsep` together
with a support point in `V₀ ⊓ V₁` gives `False`, and a conclusion-position census over the whole
project found zero producers of either separation shape.  So the separated identity's
"the DD-1c backward map satisfies it by construction" was inherited prose with nothing behind it.

The chart-typed side already retired that route.  `DivisorAdaptation.deg_presentationDivisor`
(`Picard/DivisorFamilyFieldCRT.lean:324`) proves the identity for **every** adaptation, with no
separation hypothesis at all, by evaluating the glued equalizer at stalks over the support
(`gluedStalkEval` bijective) instead of decomposing it over the cover.  This file ports that
route, which is the one a consumer should use.

## Why this port is cheaper than it looks

The stalk route touches the cover *less* than the separated route did, not more.  Measured:
`Picard/DivisorFamilyStalkEval.lean` contains **zero** chart-specific tokens, and
`Picard/DivisorFamilyFieldCRT.lean` contains exactly four, all inside one block
(`:181-184`) whose entire output is "every point lies in some piece" — the same
`AffCoverData.exists_mem_pieces` substitution that carried the separated port.  Every member the
engine reads (`pieces`, `index`, `eqn`, `eqn_regular`, `colength`, `ovlColength`, `ovlIdeal`,
`chartProd`, `Glued`, `gluedSubmodule`, `mem_gluedSubmodule_iff`) is carried by `AffAdaptation`
under the same name.

## Main declarations

* `AffAdaptation.span_germ_eqn_eq_stalkIdeal` — a piece equation generates `d`'s stalk ideal at
  each of its points, so the piece-local data is adaptation-free at stalks.
* `AffAdaptation.isUnit_germ_eqn_of_coeffAt_eq_zero` — vanishing coefficient means unit germ.
* `AffAdaptation.stalkColEval`, `stalkColEval_mk` — the piece colength evaluated at a stalk.
* `AffAdaptation.deg_presentationDivisor` — **the identity with no `hsep`**, for every widened
  adaptation.
* `AffAdaptation.IsCertified.deg_presentationDivisor` — `deg D = n`, unconditionally on the cover.

## What this does NOT close

`hdegAff` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffAbel.lean`) is the *Abel-value* ledger and remains an explicit
hypothesis there; the distance to it is the widened transport from the presentation divisor's
degree to the Picard class.  Nothing here touches `rep` or any antecedent of the atlas assembly.
-/

12	
13	The chart-independent local apparatus behind the general colength↔degree identity
14	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyFieldCRT`): over the field `K`, the colength
15	modules of a divisor adaptation evaluate into the stalk quotients `𝒪_z ⧸ I_d(z)` cut by the
16	(adaptation-free) stalk ideals of `d` — the local models of the CRT decomposition of the
17	glued equalizer `W(d)`.

340	      = coeffAt hzg (Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation) :=

9	/-!
10	# The general colength↔degree identity over a field (the Mayer–Vietoris wall, I-0179)
11	
12	For an ARBITRARY divisor adaptation `A` of a local-equation system `d` on the relative curve
13	over a field `K` — no support-separation hypothesis — this file proves
14	
15	`deg K (div d) = finrank K W(d)`   (`DivisorAdaptation.deg_presentationDivisor`),
16	
17	the general colength↔degree identity threaded as `hdeg` through the G-1 keystones
18	(`Picard/DivisorThetaFibreData.lean`) and the field dictionary
19	(`divFamFieldEquivOfDegOfSurj`, `Picard/DivisorFamilyFieldEquiv.lean`).
20	
21	## The CRT route (why the wall falls)
22	
23	The glued equalizer `W(d) ⊆ Π_j Γ(D(h_j))/(f_j)` does not decompose over the cover naively —
24	a supported point may be seen by several pieces.  The resolution
25	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyStalkEval`): decompose into **stalk** quotients
26	`𝒪_z ⧸ I_d(z)`, which are chart-independent — on the equalizer, every piece seeing `z`
27	reads the same stalk value (`stalkColEval_glued`).  Then:
28	
29	* per piece, `Γ(D(h_j))/(f_j) ≅ Π_{z ∈ supp ∩ D(h_j)} 𝒪_z ⧸ I_d(z)`
30	  (`pieceStalkEval_bijective`): injectivity is the stalk-locality of regular principal
31	  ideals (`Scheme.mem_span_singleton_of_forall_germ`), surjectivity is a dimension count —
32	  the landed per-piece degree reading (`finrank_colength_eq_sum`) against the pointwise
33	  stalk dictionary (`finrank_stalkQuot_eq_coeffAt_mul`), an honest CRT with no new
34	  constructions;
35	* globally, `W(d) ≅ Π_{z ∈ supp} 𝒪_z ⧸ I_d(z)` (`gluedStalkEval_injective` +
36	  `gluedStalkEval_surjective`): the equalizer condition makes the per-piece local values
37	  agree at shared points, and conversely any family of stalk values assembles to an
38	  equalizer element piece by piece.
39	
40	Summing `finrank K (𝒪_z ⧸ I_d(z)) = coeff_z(D) · [κ(z) : K]` over the support gives the
41	degree.  Since the left-hand side `deg K (div d)` is adaptation-free and the identity holds
42	for EVERY adaptation of `d`, adaptation-independence of the glued rank is a corollary, not
43	an input — the circularity of the refine-to-separated shortcut (I-0179) is dissolved.
44	
45	## Consequences
46	
47	* `deg_divFamDivisor` — `deg K (divFamDivisor F) = n` for every certified family
48	  `F : DivFam C K π n` (the `hdeg` input of `divFamFieldEquivOfDegOfSurj`, unconditional).
49	* `DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified.deg_presentationDivisor` — the field-level seam shape.
50	* `DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified.deg_presentationDivisor_pulledEquations` — the exact
51	  fibrewise form consumed by G-1: for a certified adaptation over any test ring, the divisor
52	  cut on the `K`-fibre by the pulled equations has degree `n` (certificates base-change,
53	  `isCertified_pullback`).
54	-/

255	    rintro ⟨i, j⟩

263	            (((relCurve C K).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom tj)

268	        Ideal.span_mono (Set.singleton_subset_iff.mpr (Set.mem_insert _ _))

272	      · by_cases hsupp : (⟨z, hzg⟩ : {x : relCurve C K // x ≠ genericPoint (relCurve C K)})
273	            ∈ (Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation).support
274	        · right
275	          have h1 : Ideal.Quotient.mk (d.stalkIdeal z)
276	              (((relCurve C K).presheaf.germ (A.pieces i) z hz.1).hom ti)
277	              = a ⟨⟨z, hzg⟩, hsupp⟩ := by
278	            have h := hval i ⟨z, hzg⟩ hsupp hz.1
279	            rw [← hti, A.stalkColEval_mk i hz.1 ti] at h
280	            exact h

284	            have h := hval j ⟨z, hzg⟩ hsupp hz.2
285	            rw [← htj, A.stalkColEval_mk j hz.2 tj] at h
286	            exact h
287	          have hdiff : ((relCurve C K).presheaf.germ (A.pieces i) z hz.1).hom ti
288	              - ((relCurve C K).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j) z hz.2).hom tj
289	              ∈ d.stalkIdeal z := by

291	          simp only [relResAlgHom_apply]
292	          rw [map_sub, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply,
293	            TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, A.span_germ_eqn_eq_stalkIdeal i hz.1]
294	          exact hdiff

298	          by_contra hc

301	        absurd (Scheme.genericPoint_mem_of_nonempty ⟨x, hx⟩) hη
302	      haveI : Subsingleton Γ(relCurve C K, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) :=

312	/-! ## The general colength↔degree identity -/
313	
314	/-- **The general colength↔degree identity** (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §3 (f), the
315	Mayer–Vietoris wall of I-0179, general case): for EVERY divisor adaptation `A` of `d` over
316	the field `K` — no support-separation hypothesis —
317	
318	`deg K (div d) = finrank K W(d)`.
319	
320	The glued equalizer is the product of the stalk colengths over the support
321	(`gluedStalkEval` bijective), and each stalk colength reads the local degree
322	(`finrank_stalkQuot_eq_coeffAt_mul`).  Since the left-hand side is adaptation-free,
323	adaptation-independence of the glued rank is a corollary. -/
324	theorem deg_presentationDivisor :
325	    Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg K (Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation)
326	      = (finrank K A.Glued : ℤ) := by
327	  have e :
328	      A.Glued ≃ₗ[K]
329	        ∀ p : {p // p ∈ (Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation).support},
330	          ((relCurve C K).presheaf.stalk p.1.1 ⧸ d.stalkIdeal p.1.1) :=
331	    LinearEquiv.ofBijective A.gluedStalkEval
332	      ⟨A.gluedStalkEval_injective, A.gluedStalkEval_surjective⟩
333	  haveI : ∀ p : {p // p ∈ (Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation).support},
334	      Module.Finite K ((relCurve C K).presheaf.stalk p.1.1 ⧸ d.stalkIdeal p.1.1) :=
335	    fun p => A.moduleFinite_stalkQuot (A.exists_mem_pieces p.1.1).choose
336	      (A.exists_mem_pieces p.1.1).choose_spec p.1.2
337	  haveI : ∀ p : {p // p ∈ (Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation).support},
338	      Module.Free K ((relCurve C K).presheaf.stalk p.1.1 ⧸ d.stalkIdeal p.1.1) :=
339	    fun p => Module.Free.of_divisionRing _ _
340	  calc Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg K (Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation)
341	      = ∑ p ∈ (Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation).support,
342	          coeffAt p.2 (Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation)
343	            * ((relCurve C K).residueDeg K p.1 : ℤ) :=
344	        Finset.sum_congr rfl fun p _ => rfl
345	    _ = ∑ p ∈ (Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation).support,
346	          (finrank K ((relCurve C K).presheaf.stalk p.1 ⧸ d.stalkIdeal p.1) : ℤ) :=
347	        Finset.sum_congr rfl fun p _ =>
348	          (A.finrank_stalkQuot_eq_coeffAt_mul (A.exists_mem_pieces p.1).choose
349	            (A.exists_mem_pieces p.1).choose_spec p.2).symm
350	    _ = ((∑ p ∈ (Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation).support,
351	          finrank K ((relCurve C K).presheaf.stalk p.1 ⧸ d.stalkIdeal p.1) : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
352	        rw [Nat.cast_sum]
353	    _ = ((finrank K
354	          (∀ p : {p // p ∈ (Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation).support},
355	            ((relCurve C K).presheaf.stalk p.1.1 ⧸ d.stalkIdeal p.1.1)) : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
356	        rw [Module.finrank_pi_fintype K, Finset.sum_coe_sort
357	          (Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation).support
358	          (fun q : {x : relCurve C K // x ≠ genericPoint (relCurve C K)} =>
359	            finrank K ((relCurve C K).presheaf.stalk q.1 ⧸ d.stalkIdeal q.1))]
360	    _ = (finrank K A.Glued : ℤ) := by rw [← e.finrank_eq]
361	
362	/-- **The degree of a certified adaptation is its rank** — the field-level `hdeg` seam
363	shape: combining the general colength↔degree identity with the field half of the
364	certificate (`IsCertified.finrank_glued`). -/
365	theorem IsCertified.deg_presentationDivisor {n : ℕ} (hc : A.IsCertified n) :
366	    Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg K (Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation) = (n : ℤ) := by
367	  rw [A.deg_presentationDivisor, hc.finrank_glued]
368	
369	end DivisorAdaptation
370	
371	/-- **The degree of a certified family is its rank** (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §3 (f),
372	UNCONDITIONAL): `deg K (divFamDivisor F) = n` for every certified divisor family, with no
373	support-separation hypothesis — the `hdeg` input of `divFamFieldEquivOfDegOfSurj`
374	(`Picard/DivisorFamilyFieldEquiv.lean`), discharged.  Supersedes
375	`deg_divFamDivisor_of_separated`. -/
376	theorem deg_divFamDivisor {n : ℕ} (F : DivFam C K π n) :
377	    Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg K (divFamDivisor F) = (n : ℤ) := by
378	  induction F using Quotient.ind with
379	  | _ G =>
380	    change Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg K (divFamDivisor (DivFam.mk G)) = (n : ℤ)
381	    rw [divFamDivisor_mk, G.adaptation.deg_presentationDivisor, G.certified.finrank_glued]
382	
383	/-! ## Discharge of the G-1 `hdeg` seam -/
384	
385	namespace DivisorAdaptation
386	
387	section PulledSeam
388	
389	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] [Algebra R K] [IsScalarTower k R K]
390	
391	/-- **The fibre degree law of a certified adaptation** — the exact `hdeg` seam shape of the
392	G-1 keystones (`Picard/DivisorThetaFibreData.lean`): for a certified adaptation over any
393	test ring and any field-valued point `R → K`, the divisor cut on the `K`-fibre by the
394	pulled equations has degree exactly the certificate rank.  Certificates base-change
395	(`isCertified_pullback`), and the general colength↔degree identity applies to the pulled
396	adaptation over the field. -/
397	theorem IsCertified.deg_presentationDivisor_pulledEquations
398	    {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations} {A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d} {n : ℕ}
399	    (hc : A.IsCertified n) :
400	    Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg K (Scheme.presentationDivisor K
401	      ((A.pulledEquations K hc.projective_colength).presentation)) = (n : ℤ) := by
402	  have h := (A.pullback K hc.projective_colength).deg_presentationDivisor
403	  rwa [(A.isCertified_pullback K hc).finrank_glued] at h
404	
405	end PulledSeam

9	/-!
10	# The widened cover datum: arbitrary affine opens (R2, human decision I-0492)
11	
12	`FinCoverData` (`Picard/DivisorFamily.lean`) types its pieces INTO a fixed pair of pinned
13	`P¹` charts — `h₀ : Fin m₀ → Γ(V₀)`, `h₁ : Fin m₁ → Γ(V₁)`, `pieces = Sum.elim (basicOpen ∘
14	h₀) (basicOpen ∘ h₁)` — with a partition of unity on EACH chart.  Per-piece swallow-or-miss
15	needs only openness (`DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean`), and it is the chart-wise partitions that
16	upgrade "inside one piece" to "inside one chart"; that upgrade is the obstruction, and no
17	repair keeping the pieces inside the preimages of a fixed pair of points of `P¹` can work
18	(`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 3 §2, ADDENDUM 4 §4.4).
19	
20	This file carries the widened datum.  A piece is an **arbitrary affine open** of the
21	relative curve, the index is a bare `Fin m`, and the covering condition is **joint**
22	(`⨆ j, pieces j = ⊤`) rather than chart-wise.  Nothing types a piece into a chart.
23	
24	Justification for the shape, used and not re-derived (I-0492 clause 2): `supp D` is finite
25	over `R`, hence lies in a single affine open of `C ×_k Spec R` (Stacks `0B8B`), so a cover
26	with one straddling piece always exists.
27	
28	## What the widening RELOCATES rather than removes (I-0492 clause 4(ii))
29	
30	The old typing was silently supplying two things that now have to be earned:
31	
32	* **every point lies in a piece** — was `relCover_sup` plus the two partitions; now it is
33	  exactly the joint covering field (`AffCoverData.exists_mem_pieces`);
34	* **`Γ(pieces j)` is `R`-flat** — was `flat_sections_basicOpen` over
35	  `flat_sections_relPinnedChart`, i.e. it rested on `Γ(V_bᴿ) ≅ R ⊗[k] Γ(C, V_b)` being FREE.
36	  For an arbitrary affine open that route is gone.  Replacement, and it is the one genuinely
37	  new commutative-algebra input the widening costs: `relCurve C R ↘ Spec R` is flat (it is
38	  the base change of `C.hom` along `overSpec k R`, and a morphism to a field spectrum is
39	  flat), and a flat morphism has `R`-flat sections on every affine open
40	  (`flat_sections_of_flat_hom`).  Unconditional in `R` — no Noetherian, no finiteness.
41	
42	Fibrewise-finite support (I-0492 clause 4(i)) is deliberately NOT here: it is not a property
43	of a cover, it must come from the seed's own degree data, and it may not hide inside a
44	`LocalEquations` or an adaptation field.
45	
46	## Main declarations
47	
48	* `AlgebraicGeometry.flat_sections_of_flat_hom` — sections of an arbitrary affine open of a
49	  scheme flat over the base ring are flat.
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.instFlatRelCurveHom` — the relative curve is flat over its test base.
51	* `AlgebraicGeometry.AffCoverData` — the widened cover datum.
52	* `AffCoverData.exists_mem_pieces`, `isAffineOpen_pieces`, `flat_sections_pieces`,
53	  `flat_sections_pieces_inf` — the derived replacements for what the chart typing supplied.
54	* `AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData.toAffCoverData` — the migration: old data instantiates the
55	  widened datum, so nothing landed becomes unreachable.
56	-/

71	
72	The engine that replaces the pinned-chart freeness argument. -/

74	section FlatSections
75	
76	variable (K : Type u) [CommRing K] (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of K))]
77	
78	/-- **Sections of an arbitrary affine open are flat, for a scheme flat over the base ring.**
79	`Scheme.overAlgebraMap` factors as `ΓSpecIso.inv` followed by the structure morphism's
80	`appLE ⊤ V`; the second is `RingHom.Flat` because `AlgebraicGeometry.Flat` is a
81	`HasRingHomProperty` for `RingHom.Flat` and `V` is affine, the first is flat because it is a
82	ring isomorphism, and `RingHom.Flat` composes.
83	
84	This is the widened replacement for `flat_sections_basicOpen ∘ flat_sections_relPinnedChart`:
85	that pair needed the open to be a basic open of a chart whose sections are a FREE base
86	change, which is exactly what an arbitrary affine open does not give. -/
87	theorem flat_sections_of_flat_hom [AlgebraicGeometry.Flat (X ↘ Spec (.of K))]
88	    {V : X.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
89	    Module.Flat K Γ(X, V) := by
90	  have happ : RingHom.Flat ((X ↘ Spec (.of K)).appLE ⊤ V (by simp)).hom :=
91	    HasRingHomProperty.appLE (P := @AlgebraicGeometry.Flat)
92	      (f := X ↘ Spec (.of K)) inferInstance ⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top _⟩ ⟨V, hV⟩ (by simp)
93	  have hiso : RingHom.Flat ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv).hom :=
94	    RingHom.Flat.of_bijective
95	      (ConcreteCategory.bijective_of_isIso (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv)
96	  have hcomp : RingHom.Flat (X.overAlgebraMap K V) := by
97	    have hfac : X.overAlgebraMap K V
98	        = ((X ↘ Spec (.of K)).appLE ⊤ V (by simp)).hom.comp
99	            ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv).hom := by
100	      rw [Scheme.overAlgebraMap, Scheme.Hom.appLE]
101	      rfl
102	    rw [hfac]
103	    exact RingHom.Flat.comp hiso happ
104	  exact (RingHom.flat_algebraMap_iff (R := K) (S := Γ(X, V))).mp hcomp
105	
106	end FlatSections

108	section RelCurveFlat
109	
110	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
111	variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
112	
113	/-- **The relative curve is flat over its test base.** `(snd C (overSpec k R)).left` is the
114	base change of `C.hom` along `(overSpec k R).hom` (`Over.isPullback_left`), and every
115	structure morphism to the spectrum of a field is flat (`flat_hom_over_field`). -/
116	instance instFlatRelCurveHom : AlgebraicGeometry.Flat (relCurve C R ↘ Spec (.of R)) :=
117	  AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.isStableUnderBaseChange.of_isPullback
118	    (Over.isPullback_left C (overSpec k R)) inferInstance
119	
120	/-- **Flat sections on an arbitrary affine open of the relative curve** — the widened
121	(c1)-flatness input, with no chart and no freeness. -/
122	theorem flat_sections_isAffineOpen {V : (relCurve C R).Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
123	    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, V) :=
124	  flat_sections_of_flat_hom R (relCurve C R) hV
125	
126	end RelCurveFlat

128	/-! ## The widened cover datum -/
129	
130	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
131	variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
132	variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k)
133	
134	/-- **The widened cover datum** (R2, human decision I-0492): finitely many **arbitrary
135	affine opens** of the relative curve that **jointly** cover it.
136	
137	Contrast with `FinCoverData`, which this replaces on the certificate side: there is no `h₀`,
138	no `h₁`, no `a₀`/`a₁`, no `partition₀`/`partition₁`, no `Sum` index, and above all no typing
139	of a piece into a pinned chart.  The chart-wise partitions of unity are exactly what upgraded
140	per-piece swallow-or-miss to a chart statement, and they are gone deliberately; the two-chart
141	structure the Θ-layer needs is carried separately (see `ChartTyping` below), never by the
142	certificate clauses.
143	
144	`Type u`, like `FinCoverData`, so a functor value can quotient it. -/
145	structure AffCoverData : Type u where
146	  /-- The number of pieces. -/
147	  m : ℕ
148	  /-- The pieces: arbitrary opens of the relative curve, made affine by `isAffineOpen`. -/
149	  pieces : Fin m → (relCurve C R).Opens
150	  /-- Every piece is affine — the only geometric demand the certificate layer makes. -/
151	  isAffineOpen : ∀ j, IsAffineOpen (pieces j)
152	  /-- The pieces cover the curve JOINTLY.  This replaces the two chart-wise partitions of
153	  unity, and it is the whole structural content of the widening. -/
154	  cover : (⨆ j, pieces j) = ⊤
155	
156	namespace AffCoverData
157	
158	variable {C R π} (D : AffCoverData C R)
159	
160	/-- The gluing index of the widened datum: a bare `Fin`, with no two-sided structure. -/
161	abbrev index : Type := Fin D.m
162	
163	/-- **Every point lies in a piece.** Under `FinCoverData` this came from `relCover_sup`
164	together with the two partitions of unity; here it is exactly the joint covering field —
165	obligation I-0492 4(ii) discharged in one line rather than silently supplied by the typing. -/
166	lemma exists_mem_pieces (z : relCurve C R) : ∃ j : D.index, z ∈ D.pieces j := by
167	  have hz : z ∈ (⨆ j, D.pieces j) := by rw [D.cover]; trivial
168	  exact Opens.mem_iSup.mp hz
169	
170	/-- The pieces are affine opens — by fiat now, rather than as basic opens of an affine
171	chart. -/
172	lemma isAffineOpen_pieces (j : D.index) : IsAffineOpen (D.pieces j) :=
173	  D.isAffineOpen j
174	
175	/-- **Flatness of the piece section rings over the test ring.** The widened replacement for
176	`FinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces`, which localized a FREE pinned-chart ring; here it is the
177	flat structure morphism of the relative curve read on an affine open. -/
178	theorem flat_sections_pieces (j : D.index) :
179	    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) :=
180	  flat_sections_isAffineOpen C R (D.isAffineOpen j)
181	
182	/-- Piece overlaps are affine (the relative curve is separated over `Spec R`, being proper),
183	so the overlap section rings are flat too — the widened
184	`FinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces_inf`. -/
185	theorem flat_sections_pieces_inf (i j : D.index)
186	    (hinf : IsAffineOpen (D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)) :
187	    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) :=
188	  flat_sections_isAffineOpen C R hinf
189	
190	end AffCoverData
191	
192	/-! ## The optional chart typing, for the Θ-layer only -/
193	
194	/-- The pinned chart of a given side, spelled here so this file needs no import from the
195	Θ-layer (it agrees with `relPinnedChart` by `rfl`). -/
196	noncomputable def pinnedChartOfSide [IsAffineHom π] (b : Bool) : (relCurve C R).Opens :=
197	  bif b then (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ else (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
198	
199	/-- **A chart typing of a widened cover**: an assignment of each piece to one of the two
200	pinned `P¹` charts, containing it.  This is what the Θ-twisting unit genuinely needs (the
201	theta cocycle lives on `V₀ ⊓ V₁`), and it is deliberately a SEPARATE datum: no certificate
202	clause and no locally-certified predicate may require it.  Keeping it separate is what stops
203	the old fixed-pair typing from being smuggled back in through a field. -/
204	structure ChartTyping [IsAffineHom π] (D : AffCoverData C R) where
205	  /-- Which pinned chart the piece is assigned to. -/
206	  side : D.index → Bool
207	  /-- The piece is contained in its assigned chart. -/
208	  piece_le : ∀ j, D.pieces j ≤ pinnedChartOfSide C R π (side j)
209	
210	/-! ## Migration: old cover data instantiates the widened datum -/
211	
212	namespace FinCoverData
213	
214	variable {C R π} [IsAffineHom π] (D : FinCoverData C R π)
215	
216	/-- **The migration map.** An old chart-typed `FinCoverData` gives a widened
217	`AffCoverData`: reindex `Fin m₀ ⊕ Fin m₁` through `finSumFinEquiv`, the pieces are affine as
218	basic opens of the affine pinned charts, and the joint cover follows from the two chart-wise
219	covers together with `relCover_sup`.
220	
221	The point of this lemma is that widening costs nothing landed: every existing construction of
222	cover data still produces a legal widened datum.  The converse fails, and that is exactly the
223	content of R2. -/
224	noncomputable def toAffCoverData : AffCoverData C R where
225	  m := D.m₀ + D.m₁
226	  pieces := fun j => D.pieces (finSumFinEquiv.symm j)
227	  isAffineOpen := fun j => by
228	    rcases finSumFinEquiv.symm j with i | i
229	    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inl]
230	      exact (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).basicOpen _
231	    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inr]
232	      exact (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).basicOpen _
233	  cover := by
234	    refine top_le_iff.mp fun z _ => ?_
235	    -- every point is in a pinned chart, and each chart is covered by its own pieces
236	    have hz : z ∈ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
237	        ⊔ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ := by
238	      rw [relCover_sup]; trivial
239	    have key : ∃ i : D.index, z ∈ D.pieces i := by
240	      rcases Opens.mem_sup.mp hz with h | h
241	      · obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (D.cover₀ h)
242	        exact ⟨Sum.inl i, hi⟩
243	      · obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp (D.cover₁ h)
244	        exact ⟨Sum.inr i, hi⟩
245	    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := key
246	    exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨finSumFinEquiv i, by
247	      simpa only [Equiv.symm_apply_apply] using hi⟩
248	
249	@[simp]
250	lemma toAffCoverData_pieces (j : Fin (D.m₀ + D.m₁)) :
251	    D.toAffCoverData.pieces j = D.pieces (finSumFinEquiv.symm j) := rfl
252	
253	/-- The canonical chart typing of a migrated datum: chart-0 pieces are basic opens of `V₀`,
254	chart-1 pieces of `V₁`. -/
255	noncomputable def toChartTyping : ChartTyping C R π D.toAffCoverData where
256	  side := fun j => (finSumFinEquiv.symm j).isRight
257	  piece_le := fun j => by
258	    rw [toAffCoverData_pieces]
259	    rcases h : finSumFinEquiv.symm j with i | i
260	    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inl]
261	      exact (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (D.h₀ i)
262	    · rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inr]
263	      exact (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (D.h₁ i)
264	
265	end FinCoverData

78	  eqn : ∀ j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)
79	  /-- The equations refine `d` pointwise up to units. -/

82	      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
83	        = (u : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y))

99	    (eqn : ∀ j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
100	    (pt : D.index → relCurve C R)
101	    (piece_le : ∀ j, D.pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j))
102	    (unit : ∀ j, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)ˣ)
103	    (eqn_eq : ∀ j, eqn j = (unit j : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
104	      * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (piece_le j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j))) :
105	    AffAdaptation D d where
106	  eqn := eqn
107	  eqn_rel := fun j y => by

109	        ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y :=
110	      inf_le_inf (piece_le j) le_rfl
111	    have E1 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
112	      (inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (eqn_eq j)
113	    rw [map_mul, res_res'] at E1
114	    have E2 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE hWle).op).hom
115	      (d.eqn_restrict_eq (pt j) y)

117	    refine ⟨(relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)
118	      * (relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y), ?_⟩
119	    rw [Units.val_mul]
120	    calc ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
121	        = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
122	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
123	              ((inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j).trans
124	                (piece_le j))).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j)) := by
125	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
126	              D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j) (unit j)).val
127	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
128	                  D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (unit j).val
129	            from rfl]

132	          * (((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
133	            * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (hWle.trans
134	                (inf_le_right : d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y
135	                  ≤ d.cover.opens y))).op).hom (d.eqn y)) := by
136	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
137	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map
138	                  (homOfLE hWle).op).hom (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y).val from rfl]
139	          rw [E2]

141	          * ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
142	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
143	              (inf_le_right : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
144	                ≤ d.cover.opens y)).op).hom (d.eqn y) := by

148	theorem eqn_regular (j : D.index) (z : relCurve C R) (hz : z ∈ D.pieces j) :
149	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)

151	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := A.eqn_rel j z
152	  have hzW : z ∈ D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z := ⟨hz, d.cover.mem_opens z⟩
153	  have hgerm : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
154	      = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom
155	          (u : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z))
156	        * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens z) z
157	            (d.cover.mem_opens z)).hom (d.eqn z) := by

159	      (D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom hu
160	    rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at h

168	/-! ### The colength modules and the glued equalizer -/
169	
170	/-- The piece-local colength module `Γ(pieces j) ⧸ (f_j)`. -/
171	noncomputable abbrev colength (j : D.index) : Type u :=
172	  Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) ⧸ Ideal.span {A.eqn j}
173	
174	/-- The symmetric overlap ideal, generated by both restricted equations. -/
175	noncomputable abbrev ovlIdeal (i j : D.index) :
176	    Ideal Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) :=
177	  Ideal.span
178	    {relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces i) (A.eqn i),
179	     relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_right : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces j) (A.eqn j)}
180	
181	/-- The overlap colength module. -/
182	noncomputable abbrev ovlColength (i j : D.index) : Type u :=
183	  Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) ⧸ A.ovlIdeal i j
184	
185	/-- Restrict-then-quotient, from the `i` component. -/
186	noncomputable def toOvlLeft (i j : D.index) : A.colength i →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
187	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn i})
188	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_left))
189	    (by
190	      intro a ha
191	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
192	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
193	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
194	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
195	          (inf_le_left : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces i) (A.eqn i)
196	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
197	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert _ _)
198	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
199	
200	/-- Restrict-then-quotient, from the `j` component. -/
201	noncomputable def toOvlRight (i j : D.index) : A.colength j →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
202	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})
203	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_right))
204	    (by
205	      intro a ha
206	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
207	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
208	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
209	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
210	          (inf_le_right : D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j ≤ D.pieces j) (A.eqn j)
211	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
212	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ rfl)
213	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
214	
215	/-- The product of the piece-local colengths. -/
216	noncomputable abbrev chartProd : Type u := ∀ j : D.index, A.colength j
217	
218	/-- The product of the overlap colengths over ordered index pairs. -/
219	noncomputable abbrev ovlProd : Type u := ∀ p : D.index × D.index, A.ovlColength p.1 p.2
220	
221	/-- The left arrow of the equalizer. -/
222	noncomputable def deltaLeft : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
223	  LinearMap.pi
224	    (fun p : D.index × D.index => (A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.1)
225	
226	/-- The right arrow of the equalizer. -/
227	noncomputable def deltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
228	  LinearMap.pi
229	    (fun p : D.index × D.index => (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
230	
231	/-- **The glued colength module `W(d)`**, spelled as a kernel so the `FlatCokernel`
232	base-change keystone applies verbatim. -/
233	noncomputable def gluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
234	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)

236	/-- The equalizer description of `W(d)`. -/
237	lemma mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
238	    s ∈ A.gluedSubmodule ↔ ∀ p : D.index × D.index,
239	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1) = A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by

11	# The degree ledger on the WIDENED adaptation: `deg D = n` over arbitrary affine pieces
12	
13	The colength↔degree identity of `Picard/DivisorFamilyFieldDegree.lean`, ported from
14	`DivisorAdaptation` (pieces typed into a fixed pair of pinned `P¹` charts) to `AffAdaptation`
15	(arbitrary affine opens, human decision I-0492).  The port is **complete**: the widened
16	`deg_presentationDivisor_eq_finrank_glued` and its `deg = n` corollary are proved here, and
17	nothing in the chain remains conditional on the chart typing.
18	
19	## What the port cost, measured rather than predicted
20	
21	The board carried this as a **four**-lemma port.  It is five: the prescription omitted
22	`coeffAt_eq_toAdd_ordZ_eqn`, the coefficient dictionary that both other geometric lemmas call.
23	That is the only way the estimate was wrong, and it was wrong in the cheap direction — not one
24	proof step of any of the five differs from its chart-typed original.
25	
26	Two substitutions carry the entire widening, and both replace a *derivation* by a structure
27	**field**:
28	
29	* `DivisorAdaptation.isAffineOpen_pieces` is a two-case `rcases` on the `Sum` index proving each
30	  piece is a basic open of a pinned affine chart; `AffCoverData.isAffineOpen_pieces` is the field.
31	  The keystone that consumes it, `finrank_quotient_span_section`
32	  (`RiemannRoch/ChartColength.lean`, in `AlgebraicGeometry` with no further namespace), takes
33	  `IsAffineOpen V` as an *argument* — it never wanted a chart.
34	* the three-line `relCover_sup` + `cover₀`/`cover₁` block inside the assembly produces exactly
35	  `∃ j, p.1 ∈ pieces j`; widened, that is `AffCoverData.exists_mem_pieces`, the joint covering
36	  field.
37	
38	So the pinned pair was never load-bearing for the degree ledger.  It was the chart-typed **cost**
39	of two facts `AffCoverData` assumes, which is why an earlier pricing of this port as *obstructed*
40	by the covering was backwards (retracted at `Picard/DivisorFamilyAffAbel.lean`, issue I-1098).
41	
42	## Main declarations
43	
44	* `AffAdaptation.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated`, `finrank_glued_eq_sum_of_separated` — the
45	  algebraic half: separation collapses the equalizer to the product, and Mayer–Vietoris finrank
46	  additivity with no overlap correction.
47	* `AffAdaptation.coeffAt_eq_toAdd_ordZ_eqn` — the coefficient dictionary (the fifth lemma).
48	* `AffAdaptation.finrank_colength_eq_sum` — the per-piece degree reading, on an arbitrary affine
49	  piece.
50	* `AffAdaptation.coeffAt_eq_zero_of_isUnit_germ`, `subsingleton_ovlColength_of_sep` — the
51	  separation inputs.
52	* `AffAdaptation.deg_presentationDivisor_eq_finrank_glued` — the geometric half.
53	* `AffAdaptation.IsCertified.finrank_glued` — the field half.
54	* `AffAdaptation.deg_presentationDivisor_eq_of_isCertified` — `deg D = n`.
55	* `DivisorAdaptation.sep_toAff`, `exists_widened_deg_eq_of_certifiedFamily_sep` — the joint

57	
58	## What is NOT closed by this file
59	
60	`hdegAff` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffAbel.lean`) is the *Abel-value* ledger — the widened Abel value

102	/-- **A nonzero principal ideal of a local Dedekind domain (a DVR) is the count-th power of
103	the maximal ideal**: every prime factor of `(g)` is a nonzero prime, hence maximal, hence
104	*the* maximal ideal, so the factorization multiset is `count` copies of it. -/
105	theorem span_singleton_eq_maximalIdeal_pow_count {S : Type*} [CommRing S]
106	    [IsDedekindDomain S] [IsLocalRing S] {g : S} (hg : g ≠ 0) :
107	    Ideal.span {g} = maximalIdeal S
108	        ^ Multiset.count (maximalIdeal S) (factors (Ideal.span {g})) := by
109	  have hI : Ideal.span {g} ≠ ⊥ := by rwa [Ne, Ideal.span_singleton_eq_bot]
110	  have hall : ∀ P ∈ factors (Ideal.span {g}), P = maximalIdeal S := by
111	    intro P hP
112	    have hprime : Prime P := prime_of_factor _ hP
113	    haveI : P.IsPrime := Ideal.isPrime_of_prime hprime
114	    exact IsLocalRing.eq_maximalIdeal (Ideal.IsPrime.isMaximal ‹P.IsPrime› hprime.ne_zero)
115	  have hrepl : factors (Ideal.span {g})
116	      = Multiset.replicate (Multiset.card (factors (Ideal.span {g}))) (maximalIdeal S) :=
117	    Multiset.eq_replicate_card.mpr hall
118	  conv_lhs => rw [← associated_iff_eq.mp (factors_prod hI)]
119	  rw [hrepl, Multiset.prod_replicate, Multiset.count_replicate_self]
